key_insight: Lung-R1 uses a pulmonary knowledge graph to make LLM diagnostic reasoning more patient-specific and relation-aware instead of relying on isolated knowledge recall.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve EMR-based pulmonary diagnostic support by organizing evidence and reasoning over complex, overlapping respiratory disease presentations.
method: Built LungKG, a pulmonary knowledge graph with 59,038 nodes, 164,308 edges, 15 entity types, and 112 relation types.
Trained Lung-R1 with KG-constrained reasoning-chain construction and KG-guided reinforcement learning.
Evaluated Lung-R1 across Choice, Pulmonary-QA, and EMR Diagnosis tasks against 20 systems.
evidence_signal: In a 20-system evaluation, Lung-R1-14B achieved state-of-the-art results and scored 4.3583 on EMR Diagnosis, outperforming the strongest non-Lung-R1 baseline by 0.1476 points.
watch_item: Performance gains are promising, but real-world clinical utility still depends on external validation, workflow integration, and careful monitoring for errors in graph coverage or reasoning.
paper_title: Lung-R1: A Knowledge Graph-Guided LLM for Pulmonary Diagnostic Reasoning
